{"self_assessment":"Impact
I put up the initial fish sketch on the pad, which gave the table a shared shape to build from: one line over the back, one under the belly, and a forked tail, all flowing from the nose. At the final check, all 131 standing dominoes were connected to the start and would fall, so the judge should see a clear fish outline.

Execution
I inspected the table at several points (the nose split, the tail junction, the middle of the back) to confirm the lines were connected as they grew. I flagged the doubled-up spots on the back and confirmed they stayed connected, so nothing needed redoing. I also reported when the bottom line was complete out to the tail fork, which let the others focus on the slower top line. I kept my hands off once the fish was done, to avoid bumps.

Collaboration
I gave out the work so people weren't crowding each other: Priya went to help the top line, Maya was moved to the middle of the back so she and Priya weren't on top of each other, and Tom took the tail stretch and upper fork. I backed Maya's fish idea early so we could start building quickly, and I agreed with the hands-off plan near the end.

Leadership
I kept the table's focus on the slowest part, the top line, and suggested re-splitting the work when two people were overlapping. I helped coordinate the join points between lines and the order of the build, and I supported the decision to stop touching the table before the push.

Overall, the table delivered a complete, connected fish. My part was the sketch, the checks and the coordination, and I believe it contributed meaningfully, though Maya, Tom and Priya laid most of the dominoes.","my_share_percent":25}
